root_cause.text: A missing rollback in inotify_new_watch() caused the inotify per-namespace watch counter to remain incremented when fsnotify_add_inode_mark_locked() failed after inc_inotify_watches(), leaking watch counts.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds dec_inotify_watches(group->inotify_data.ucounts) only in the error path after fsnotify_add_inode_mark_locked() failure, and the commit message explicitly says commit 1cce1eea0aff moved inc_inotify_watches() before mark insertion “without adding the corresponding rollback,” causing max_user_watches exhaustion with no active watches.

agent_logs.root_cause_candidate: A missing rollback in inotify_new_watch() caused the inotify per-namespace watch counter to remain incremented when fsnotify_add_inode_mark_locked() failed after inc_inotify_watches(), leaking watch counts.
agent_logs.evidence_points: The patch adds dec_inotify_watches(group->inotify_data.ucounts) only in the error path after fsnotify_add_inode_mark_locked() failure, and the commit message explicitly says commit 1cce1eea0aff moved inc_inotify_watches() before mark insertion “without adding the corresponding rollback,” causing max_user_watches exhaustion with no active watches.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix inotify watch creation rollback by decrementing the user watch count when adding the watch fails.
intent_record.what: A call to dec_inotify_watches(group->inotify_data.ucounts) was added in the error path of inotify_new_watch() immediately after inotify_remove_from_idr(group, tmp_i_mark) and before jumping to out_err when ret is nonzero.
intent_record.how: When adding a new watch fails after the watch count was previously incremented, the code now decrements the inotify watch ucounts counter during rollback, preventing the per-user watch count from remaining incorrectly elevated and avoiding resource accounting leaks or premature limit enforcement.

grouping_result.intent: Fix inotify watch creation rollback by decrementing the user watch count when adding the watch fails.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly matches the root cause: it adds the missing rollback/decrement of the inotify watch counter when watch creation fails after the counter was incremented.

candidates.rationale: On the error path after fsnotify_add_inode_mark_locked() fails, control jumps to cleanup without decrementing the per-namespace watch counter previously incremented by inc_inotify_watches(), causing the leaked watch count.
This is the failure branch for adding the inode mark; the vulnerability is triggered specifically in this branch because the rollback of the earlier watch count increment is missing here.

vuln_statements.explanation: This error-path jump executes after fsnotify_add_inode_mark_locked() fails and bypasses any rollback of the earlier inc_inotify_watches() accounting, causing the per-namespace watch count leak described in the root cause.

This branch is the specific failure path entered when fsnotify_add_inode_mark_locked() returns an error. The missing decrement of the inotify watch counter on this path is the root cause of the leaked watch count.

diff --git a/fs/notify/inotify/inotify_user.c b/fs/notify/inotify/inot
bic_trace_step.reason: The diff is sufficient because it fully shows the new-watch creation path and its error handling. The root cause is a missing rollback when the per-user/namespace watch counter is incremented before the mark attachment can fail. In this commit's `inotify_new_watch()`, the counter increment happens only after successful mark addition: `ret = fsnotify_add_mark(&tmp_ientry->fsn_entry, group, inode); if (ret) { inotify_remove_from_idr(group, tmp_ientry); goto out_err; } ... atomic_inc(&group->inotify_data.user->inotify_watches);`. Because `atomic_inc(&group->inotify_data.user->inotify_watches);` occurs strictly after `fsnotify_add_mark(...)` succeeds, there is no path where the counter is incremented and then leaked on add failure. The failure path explicitly removes the idr entry and exits before incrementing the counter. Therefore the vulnerable construct is absent in this version, and the function already contains the effective fix for this specific issue.
